_comment: EXAMPLE ONLY — copy to power.json and replace EVERY number with your own install's. `pbz limit --for-budget --set` writes a hardware brightness cap derived from these figures; running it against someone else's numbers gives you a cap that has nothing to do with your wiring. The values below are from one real 170-pixel WRGB ring on a 160 W 24 V brick, kept as a worked example of the shape rather than a default worth inheriting.

protection_chain._comment: Every series link between the supply and the LEDs, in amps. The effective budget is the SMALLEST of these — the solver reports which one binds. Add or drop links to match your build; the names are free-form and are printed as-is by `pbz power budget`.

measured._comment: MEASURED, not from the strip's nameplate — nameplate figures are routinely optimistic. all_four_max_amps is the whole run with every channel at full, which is what a color-blind brightness cap has to assume. Meter it; don't estimate it.
measured._channel_bench_note: Each channel alone at full, 100 pixels, both ends fed. Needed by `pbz power` (the live per-pattern estimate). On an RGBW strip it models W-extraction: min(r,g,b) is routed to the dedicated white element, so a white pixel must not be counted as r+g+b. ON A PLAIN RGB STRIP, keep r/g/b and OMIT w — pbz then skips the extraction model entirely and counts all three channels, which is what an RGB strip actually draws. Do not delete the whole block; `pbz power` cannot estimate without it.

_margin_note: Applied on top of the binding link's raw share of all_four_max_amps, so the cap sits below a link's rated maximum instead of flush against it.
